city_center.landmark: Reading Terminal Market (est. 1893), one of the oldest continuously operating public markets in the US; Italian Market (9th Street) South Philly; brick rowhouse blocks
city_center.notes: Reading Terminal Market is a landmark indoor public market with Pennsylvania Dutch and regional producers. The 9th Street Italian Market is the country's oldest continuously operating outdoor market. Philadelphia's residential fabric is dense brick rowhouses. sources: readingterminalmarket.org; en.wikipedia.org Italian Market, Philadelphia.

cultural_notes: Reading Terminal Market (1893) is a civic food anchor with Pennsylvania Dutch (Amish/Mennonite) producers alongside regional farmers -- a Center City institution (source: readingterminalmarket.org; en.wikipedia.org)
the 9th Street Italian Market is the oldest continuously operating outdoor market in the US, a South Philly cultural landmark (source: en.wikipedia.org Italian Market, Philadelphia)

Lancaster County Pennsylvania Dutch farm country supplies apple butter, apples, and maple to the metro -- a strong regional food identity (source: general Pennsylvania Dutch foodways framing, publicly documented)

Philadelphia's dense brick rowhouse blocks are a defining architectural identity; Acme (a Philly-rooted chain), Giant, and ShopRite are the regional grocers (source: chain regional footprint; Philadelphia rowhouse architecture)
